productConcept.label: Memory
productConcept.modelSafeDescription: Memory is one reviewable product concept: accepted facts or cards with provenance, scope and lifecycle state. Runtime facts, role cards, embeddings and Dreaming caches are implementation data domains, not separate product memories.
productConcept.approvalBoundary: Candidates and derived signals never become accepted memory without the owning governance or runtime acceptance path. Only accepted memory may be retrieved or injected into model context.

domains.retention: Owner-managed role-memory card lifecycle; active/cold/archived/tombstone states remain explicit.
domains.deletion: Deletion and tombstoning are performed by role-memory card governance and remove retrievability.
domains.invalidation: Review, evidence, scope or version invalidation marks the card non-injectable until the owner re-accepts it.
domains.migration: Legacy role-memory SQLite cards remain in place; field normalization is applied without moving the store.

domains.retention: Runtime Memory owns fact TTL, session/run scope and eviction.
domains.deletion: Runtime Memory removes the fact and invalidates dependent usage/embedding entries.
domains.invalidation: Contradiction, stale evidence or scope mismatch invalidates the fact before retrieval.
domains.migration: Existing Runtime Memory state remains in its domain store; no forced single-database migration.

domains.retention: Timeline retention follows its owning session or run.
domains.deletion: Deleting the owning session/run removes or invalidates timeline state.
domains.invalidation: A replaced generation or invalidated episode makes the timeline stale.
domains.migration: Timeline records stay in Runtime Memory; schema changes are additive.

domains.retention: Episode retention is bounded by Runtime Memory lifecycle.
domains.deletion: Runtime Memory owns episode deletion and dependent index removal.
domains.invalidation: Lost execution context or contradiction invalidates the episode.
domains.migration: Episodes remain in Runtime Memory; retrieval indexes can be rebuilt from accepted evidence.

domains.retention: Candidate queue may persist beyond a session but is bounded by owner policy.
domains.deletion: Reject/delete removes the candidate or leaves an audit tombstone without accepted content.
domains.invalidation: Rejected, superseded or stale candidates are never promoted into retrieval.
domains.migration: Candidate records remain in the queue store and reference an accepted-memory target by identity.

domains.retention: Index lifetime follows the accepted source and embedding provider policy.
domains.deletion: Deleting an accepted source removes or rebuilds its vector entries.
domains.invalidation: Changed source digest, provider/model change or deleted source invalidates the index entry.
domains.migration: Embeddings are rebuildable derived data and are never the sole copy of memory.

domains.retention: Query receipts are transient and bounded by the request.
domains.deletion: No durable memory is created; transient query records may be discarded.
domains.invalidation: A changed source file invalidates the query result.
domains.migration: Native memory files remain read-only sources; no migration into another database is required.

domains.retention: Dreaming caches follow phase/storage policy and may be rebuilt from accepted sources.
domains.deletion: Reset/repair operations remove derived diary/cache artifacts without deleting accepted memory.
domains.invalidation: Cache input changes, duplicate repair or reset invalidates and rebuilds derived signals.
domains.migration: Dreaming remains a rebuildable derived cache; it is not migrated as accepted memory.

unmeasured: external-provider value of automatic Dreaming promotion
